key_insight: MAC is the first public conversion-rate (CVR) benchmark that supplies conversion labels under multiple attribution mechanisms, enabling multi-attribution learning (MAL) and improving CVR model robustness and comparability across attribution rules.
problem_solved: Public CVR datasets historically provide labels from only a single attribution rule, preventing research and fair evaluation of models that learn from or must generalize across different attribution mechanisms.
method: Assemble MAC: collect/generate conversion labels for the same user–event instances under multiple common attribution mechanisms (e.g., last-touch, first-touch, rule-based variants).
Provide standardized dataset splits, evaluation protocols, and baseline models to benchmark multi-attribution learning approaches.
Evaluate MAL approaches vs. single-label baselines to demonstrate gains in prediction robustness and generalization when training with multiple attribution labels.
impact: MAC enables researchers and practitioners to develop and fairly compare models that account for attribution uncertainty, leading to more robust CVR predictions and better-informed ad optimization when attribution policies vary in production.
visual_elements: Sankey or flow diagram mapping user touchpoints to different attribution mechanisms and the resulting label differences.
Bar chart comparing model performance (AUC/LogLoss) of MAL-trained models vs. single-attribution baselines across multiple attribution test sets.
Dataset composition infographic showing counts/ratios of conversions per attribution mechanism and available features.
Pipeline diagram: multi-attribution label generation → training strategies (multi-task/ensemble/label-aggregation) → deployment implications.
paper_title: MAC: A Conversion Rate Prediction Benchmark Featuring Labels Under Multiple Attribution Mechanisms
paper_authors: Jinqi Wu, Sishuo Chen, Zhangming Chan, Yong Bai, Lei Zhang
